(The game will lookahead to see if your declared path will actually result in movement, ignoring all triggered abilities but considering all ongoing effects.) Alternately, Skirmishers may shoot when they enter a new location during basic movement. They get one shot total during their basic movement, regardless of how far they move.
Note that basic movement includes movement from a basic ability, i.e. Move and Attack, and Defend.

question: Is this an activated ability that I use while Slimy Mutants are in my hand?
answer: Yes! While Slimy Mutants are in your hand, you may pay (3) and resolve the effect.

question: If attacked by a minion that strikes first, does the Giantess end up striking back?
answer: Yes, assuming she isn't killed.

question: What happens if there are two Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby each other?
answer: See "((Example - Two Smokestacks of Gnaak))" in the codex!

question: Are minions along the path affected even if they have stealth?
answer: Yes! Projectiles do not hit stealth minions, but Snowball is just using the projectile to draw a path. It doesn't matter what units are hit, all of them along the path are rolled up in the snowball and pulled along!

question: Does the snowball’s path include both the starting and ending locations?
answer: Yes! The projectile's path determines which locations are affected by the rest of the snowball, gathering up everything along the way, just as you'd expect giant snowball physics would work after watching all those Saturday morning cartoons.

question: If I happen to play a Lone Tower from the top of my atlas, will the mana from the Genesis ability also be doubled? What about mana from Abundance?
answer: Yes. Any mana that the site produces, including via any abilities, will be doubled.

question: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
answer: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell "((you))" cast, meaning the player.

question: Is the damage considered air damage?
answer: Yes.

question: If I give my Sparkmage a poisonous dagger, will it deal lethal damage with its tap ability?
answer: Yes, because it's dealing the damage directly via it's ability. (Damage from a lightning bolt cast by the Sparkmage would not be lethal.)

question: If I reduce the threshold required to cast the spell (e.g. Mix Aer), does the threshold still count for the Sparkmage ability?
answer: Yes. The Sparkmage ability considers printed threshold on the spell.

question: What if the minion being killed occupies more than one location?
answer: You choose where the spear teleports, which will be a single location the minion occupies.

question: What does "Avatars here can't leave" mean?
answer:
Avatars currently under the Sphere of Animosity can't enter locations not occupied by the Sphere. This means they can't move to those locations, or be moved by force.
Note that when a site moves, it carries along cards of normal size with it, and those cards do not count as entering a new location. This means that a moving site can carry an Avatar out of the Sphere.

question: Does Spire satisfy the Spire Lich?
answer: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

question: Does Watchtower satisfy the Spire Lich?
answer: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

question: When is the power of the minion checked to see if it's small enough to summon to any site?
answer: You check at the time of casting, before the minion enters the realm. This means that you can summon a Vengeful Heir to any site, even if it enters the realm as a minion which would be too large to work with Spore Sprouts normally, for example.

question: Let's say the Mass is 1 power, and it fights another 1 power minion. What happens?
answer: Both take 1 damage each, which results in their simultaneous death. That triggers Squirming Mass's ability, which means its gains +1 power, but it's already dying, and merely gaining power isn't enough to save it. (Something specifically that saves a unit from death would be necessary, like Gilded Aegis.) In this example, both minions are placed in the cemetery.

question: If a minion's current power is different from its printed power when it dies, which value does Squirming Mass gain?
answer: The current power of the minion that dies.

question: Can this Pick Up and carry enemy minions?
answer: Yes, the coach will carry anyone!

question: How does this ability work?
answer:
The Abomination takes damage as if it is one unit, but the player causing the damage can choose which part or parts of the Abomination it applies to (after damage reduction, if any). Once a part has enough damage assigned to kill it, it's removed. When the last part of the Abomination is destroyed, so is the Abomination.
For example, I have an Abomination with 5 + 4 + 3 power, and you are dealing it 7 damage from a Major Explosion. You can assign 3 and 4 damage, destroying those parts, and it's left with 5 power. Alternately, if it were my own Major Explosion, I could assign 3 damage to the 5-power part, and 3 damage to the 4-power part, and 1 damage to 3-power part. It's left with 5+4+3 power, with some damage on each of those parts (which will be removed normally at end of turn).

If an effect would destroy or kill the Abomination outright, including taking Lethal damage, all of its parts are killed. If an effect would banish the Abomination, all of it is banished.

question: When does this ability resolve?
answer: Whenever an enemy announces a Magic spell, after they've paid the costs but before the spell resolves.

question: What does "closer" mean?
answer:
Determine which location it could step to using its normal movement that would be closest to the caster that triggered it.
For instance, assume the Sturmgeist is at location S, and the spellcaster is at location C:
Because the Sturmgeist has the airborne ability, it is able to get from S to C in one step, so it must do so, leaving it zero steps away from the caster.  It cannot move to A or B, because those locations are still one step away from the caster, which is further than zero steps.

question: If the spellcaster dies before the spell they cast resolves, will their spell still resolve?
answer: No! If the spellcaster is dead before their spell resolves, the spell will not resolve at all. See "((Source is No Longer in the Realm))" for more details.

question: What if the Magic is cast by something other than a unit?
answer: The Sturmgeist only hears spells cast by enemies, which are units. Spells cast by artifacts (e.g. Omphalos) or sites (e.g. River of Flame) will not trigger its ability.

question: Does this allow me to summon my units burrowed even without burrowing?
answer: No. The effect only allows you to break the restriction of choosing one of your own sites, but not the rule about summoning atop the site.

question: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
answer: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

question: If one target is a minion, can the other target be an artifact, and vice versa?
answer: Yes. Target one (minion or artifact) and target another (minion or artifact).

question: How exactly do I resolve a "swap" effect?
answer: The two cards are simultaneously teleported to each other's location. If one of the targets cannot be targeted or teleported (e.g. Iron Man Talus), neither target moves.

question: Can this effect swap cards into different regions?
answer: No. You target both cards being swapped, and targets must be in the same region as the caster. See ((Casting Spells)) for more information.

question: What if one or both of the swapped cards were being carried?
answer:
If either card was being carried by a unit, that unit will be carrying the newly swapped artifact/minion, due to the golden rule.
For example, if two carried artifacts are swapped, the bearers will be carrying their newly swapped artifacts (even if they both are in the same location).
If a minion is swapped with an artifact, presumably the minion will be immediately dropped (unless the new bearer can carry minions) and the artifact will not be carried (unless the swapped minion was being carried before it was swapped).

question: What if an oversized unit is involved?
answer: Choose one of the locations the oversized unit occupies as the destination of the other card. See "((Teleporting Oversized Units))" for more details.

question: How do I resolve this effect if I sacrifice a card that has multiple types (e.g. Automaton) ?
answer: When you sacrifice a card that has multiple types, you may specify which type your opponent must match. For example, if you sacrifice one automaton (Minion and Artifact), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an artifact, your choice (not both). Similarly, if you're playing as Enchantress and you sacrifice an animated aura (Minion and Aura), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an aura, your choice (not both).

question: What is the timing for the resolution of this spell?
answer:
Choose an ally, declare its movement steps, placing them on the Storyline, then resolve those steps. Repeat for each ally.
That is, you declare and resolve each ally’s steps before proceeding to the next ally. If you gain more allies during the resolution, you may move them too; keep repeating the effect until each ally has moved.

question: Once the Thankless Squire has delivered all those lances, and isn't carrying any more, is it still Immobile?
answer: Yes, he's very tired and in need of a rest.

question: What does it mean to "build The Tower of Babel" and "play ... atop this" ?
answer:
You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel.
The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again.
For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

question: If it’s not adjacent to void and is within Abundance, does it still gain extra mana?
answer: Yes. The site doesn't provide mana normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Abundance), then it can provide additional mana. 0 + 1 = 1.

question: If it’s not adjacent to void and is the target of a flood, does it still gain water affinity?
answer: Yes. The site doesn't provide affinity normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Flood), then it will.

question: Can this minion die?
answer: The only way it can be killed is if you sacrifice it. Otherwise, it cannot be killed. Meet your doom!

question: If Draconian Bonekite, Sir Pelleas, and Azuridge Caravan are all in the realm, can I choose to keep the Caravan and another minion?
answer: No, you cannot save Azuridge Caravan and other minions. Since Azuridge Caravan counts as all minion types, you cannot save it and any other minion with a type since they will always have a shared type.

question: If there are minions with multiple types in the realm, can I choose what type they count as when resolving The Flood? (e.g. I control Draconian Bonekite and Wyvern.
answer: They are both of their minion types at all times. Though each minion has another minion type in addition to Dragon in their type line, you can only choose one! You can only save one Dragon from the flood!

question: Who chooses what minions of each type are saved from The Flood?
answer: The controller of the spell.

question: Can I choose to save a minion that has no minion type e.g. Maiden, Mother, Crone?
answer: No, since Maiden, Mother, Crone has no type it cannot be saved from being submerged.

question: If The Geistwood site itself and minions occupying the site are all destroyed at the same time, do the minions' genesis abilities still count as Deathrite abilities, or can the active player decide to destroy Geistwood before the deathrites resolve?
answer: Since the destruction is simultaneous (e.g. Roots of Ygdrassil), all Deathrites will resolve before cards are moved to the cemetery.

question: How does summoning burrowed interact with Evil Presence?
answer: You may summon the Haunts to an affected site, and they must be burrowed. But the Haunts won't gain Charge and Evil Presence will remain in the realm because the Haunts were not summoned "here" according to Evil Presence, since Evil Presence occupies the surface (and perhaps the void), not underground.

question: What does "alone here" mean?
answer: No other units at the location.

question: What counts as "playing" a card?
answer: Playing a site, which costs 0, or casting a spell.

question: If I modify the cost of a spell (e.g. a Mix artifact, or an alternate casting cost), does The Immortal Throne look at the modified cost or the printed cost?
answer: Cost in this case means "printed cost."

question: The alpha foil version has the text for Pendulum of Peril on it. Is that a misprint?
answer: Yes. Use the text for the normal version. The foil version is not legal for tournament ))play((.

question: When does this ability trigger?
answer: If an effect requires you to reveal it from your hand, or from your spellbook, or if your opponent searches your spellbook.

question: If the 3 damage is reduced, redirected away from "here", or prevented, do I still heal 3?
answer: No, the full 3 damage must be dealt to the targeted minion here in order to heal 3.

question: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?
answer:
When a site moves, only things of "normal" size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved.
In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. [[Rift Valley]]). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of [[Cloud City]], which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See ((mandatory actions)) for what happens if your avatar is in the void.
Note that in both cases the avatar does not "enter" the new location that it is occupying.

question: Stretch my avatar? You're pulling my leg! Does this make my avatar an oversized unit now?
answer: Pulling both arms and both legs actually but, yes! Your avatar will now be an oversized unit!

question: When an avatar is stretched by this effect, does it count as entering the new location?
answer: Yes! The avatar has to be able to enter the location for the effect to work, and then it will trigger any effects caused by entering. It does not count as moving, however.

question: How does this site work?
answer:
The site still has both a surface and subsurface, but those locations also count as void simultaneously. It has a surface + void location, and a subsurface + void location.
Minions without voidwalk that enter the site will be banished.
Spells cast from the surface + void location can target cards that are in the surface or the void, for example.
Projectiles can travel from the surface + void location into the void.

question: Can my avatar enter this site?
answer: Yes.

question: Can forced movement move a minion from a surface location to the surface of The Void?
answer: Yes!

question: When my opponent casts a minion spell with Voidwalk, can they choose The Void as its summoning location, even though it's my site?
answer: Yes! It is a void, so they can choose to cast their Voidwalk minions to here if they wish.

question: While my Avatar occupies the surface + void location of The Void site, can I target something occupying the underground + void location of The Void site?
answer: Yes! The target is in the same region (void) as the spellcaster, so it can be targeted!

question: Normally, when moving from void to a site, a minion (e.g. Hounds of Ondaros) can move directly to the surface OR subsurface. Therefore, when moving from the subsurface + void location of this site, can a minion like Hounds of Ondaros move directly to the surface of an adjacent site? Could they move from the surface + void location directly to the subsurface of an adjacent site?
answer: Yes! Minions with voidwalk can continue to use their voidwalk abilities to move accordingly.

question: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
answer: The beta text is correct.

question: Can Tide Naiads move from an underwater location to an underground location?
answer: No. They would need to enter the underground location to flood it, and they cannot enter underground locations without burrowing.

question: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
answer: Yes!

question: How does this work with end of turn and damage clearing?
answer: The intent is that a 1 power minion with 1 damage + the Trinket would survive the turn.

question: Do I have to reveal the traded artifacts?
answer: Yes, you must reveal them to ensure it is a fair trade.

question: What is a "lone enemy"?
answer:
A "lone enemy" is an enemy unit that's not entering simultaneously with another enemy unit. Stationary units at the Troll Bridge ignored.
Here are some examples:
- If an enemy [[War Horse]] is carrying its Avatar and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger, since there are two enemies entering simultaneously. 
- If your [[Bodach Bogeyman]] is carrying two enemy minions and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger. However, if the Bogeyman were carrying just one enemy, the Bridge would trigger.
- If there is already an enemy occupying the Troll Bridge and another enemy unit enters, it will trigger for the entering enemy.

question: Can the bearer shoot or defend against a stealthed enemy?
answer: Yes. The bearer can target stealthed minions with spells, shoot them with projectiles, attack or intercept them and even defend against their attacks.

question: My Tufted Turtles attack (having taken no damage so far this turn), and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Tufted Turtles take?
answer: 0, because all three Foot Soldiers did damage at the same time, tied for first, and thus all are prevented!

question: Does this count as healing?
answer: No, this is setting life.

question: What happens if I cast this when I’m at death’s door?
answer: You can cast it, and your opponent will go to 0 life, being put at Death’s Door and becoming immune to damage for the rest of the turn. You will still remain at 0 life since you can’t gain life once you’re at death’s door.

question: The alpha foil version has 3 air threshold and the normal version has 2 air threshold. Which is correct?
answer: The normal version is correct. You only need 2 air affinity to cast this minion.

question: When Ultimate Horror summons dead voidwalk minions, can they go to different nearby sites and voids?
answer: Yes!

question: Can it burrow and unburrow different things the same turn?
answer: Yes.

question: Does Undertow let you pull a unit underwater if they have submerge?
answer: No, because it’s a “normal step,” which doesn’t allow changing regions.

question: When it submerges, can it pull down a minion anywhere in the realm, or only from its location?
answer: No. Unland Eel can only drag a minion that shares its location.

question: If I have two Vanguard Knights equally forward, do they cancel each other out?
answer: Yes. They only get the benefit if they are the true vanguard, with a single minion being the farthest forward.

question: How do I know if they're the "farthest forward?"
answer: The row of squares closest to you is 1, then the next row is 2, then 3, then 4. The higher the number, the farther forward it is.

question: Does this prevent enemy magic from harming my beasts?
answer: Yes, as long as the effect says “target”. You’ll need to bring in a specialized exterminator to flush out these hidey-holes.

question: What counts as an "enemy" for this effect? Is it enemies of the beast, or enemies of the site?
answer: Beasts at Varmint Warrens cannot be targeted by spells or abilities used by the enemies of the beast. All kinds of critters can hide in the warrens!

question: If I choose to submerge minions and artifacts here, do I submerge Vatn Draconis too?
answer: Yes, it will submerge itself. You cannot choose to submerge only some of the minions and artifacts.

question: If I play this under my avatar, have I stopped there?
answer: No, because a unit doesn't enter the site if the unit was already present in the square when the site was played.

question: What does "stops here" mean?
answer: An avatar stops when there is no additional movement for that unit on the Storyline. A unit must first move to then stop.

question: Does Vaults of Zul trigger once per game, or once per game per avatar?
answer: Once per game total. They took time to loot the vaults! (If two avatars somehow stop on the vaults simultaneously, they will both be tied for first, and will both loot the vaults.)

question: What does it mean to "fly to" something? Does it have to be the shortest possible path or any valid path?
answer: Refer to the article on ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) to see how an ability like this works.

question: When moving sites around, does Vindictive Nation protect the nearby sites before or after the move?
answer:
Vindictive Nation protects the sites it was nearby before the move. For example:
- I = Vindictive Nation
- R = Rubble
- A = Allied Site
My opponent casts Earthquake and rearranges the two rightmost sites:
Even though site A moved and is now nearby Vindictive Nation, my opponent doesn't lose any life because A wasn't nearby Vindictive Nation before the move.
Alternately, if we started from the second situation and Earthquake moved sites into the first situation, my opponent would lose 3 life because they moved a site that was nearby Vindictive Nation (even though the site ended up no longer nearby).

question: If my Vindictive Nation is silenced by my opponent, e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak, will my opponent lose life?
answer: No, because Smokestacks silences them first. Vindictive Nation's ability is effectively a triggered ability, while Smokestacks are a passive ability that generates an ongoing effect. Ongoing effects are applied before triggered abilities can trigger.

question: Does this effect have time to resolve if the site itself is getting destroyed?
answer: Yes! They are very vindictive.

question: Does "modifying" a site include Flooding it?
answer: Yes, since Flooded is an ability that gets added to the site.

question: What does “wherever she is" mean?
answer: Anywhere! The realm, your hand, and cemetery, and even while in the middle of your spellbook.

question: Since Avatars are Spellcasters, is Vivien a Spellcaster?
answer: Not by default. Avatars don’t have the printed ability “Spellcaster,” so Vivien must gain the Spellcaster ability another way, e.g. a minion with the printed Spellcaster ability.

question: Can Vivien the Enchantress copy the abilities of another Vivien the Enchantress?
answer: No.

question: What happens if Vivien uses the Druid’s ability to summon Bruin and flip?
answer: She summons Bruin and then flips. As a flipped card with nothing on the back, she has no game text and will effectively do nothing for the rest of the game. She is no longer a minion, has no card type or abilities, etc. The flipped card can exist in the void, and technically she could turn off Pristine Paradise, and would be destroyed by Roots of Yggdrasil.

question: Does this affect subsurface units?
answer: No. (They are not atop the site.)

question: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
answer: An animated Wall of Air can’t move (unless it gains power), since it has a Wall of Air in its middle! If it gains power (or teleports) and manages to move, the Wall of Air applies between the two squares it occupies.

question: Does this affect the corners of the border? (e.g. Airborne units moving diagonally)
answer: No. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

question: How many squares does this aura occupy?
How many squares does this aura occupy?
What does “passes through” mean?
answer: Moving through in any way, whether willingly or by force. For example, a unit moved by Grapple Shot or Pudge Butcher would take damage from the Wall of Fire. Note that a teleported unit doesn’t pass through borders, and thus wouldn't be affected.

question: Does this affect Airborne units?
answer: Yes. (They are atop the site.)

question: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
answer: It can move, but units are not passing through the Wall of Flame due to its own movement. After moving, its effect will apply between the two squares it occupies.

question: Does this affect subsurface units?
answer: No. (They are not atop the site.)

question: How many squares does this aura occupy?
What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
answer: An animated Wall of Ice can’t move normally, since it has a Wall of Ice in its middle! If it gains Airborne (or teleports, etc.) and manages to move, the Wall of Ice applies between the two squares it occupies.

question: When is the power doubled?
answer: This effect applies a doubling throughout the turn. If the unit gains or loses power, apply any additions or subtractions first, then double.

question: What does "drowns" mean?
answer: A minion "drowns" if it dies due to being underwater without also having the submerge ability. You control the resulting Skeleton.

question: How do I properly resolve this effect?
answer:
Choose a cardinal direction from your water site. Forcefully move all enemies from your water site one step in the chosen direction and flood that site. Trigger and resolve any effects related to minions entering or the site being flooded. Then repeat the process until you reach the edge of the realm.
The flood and push effect will continue even across a void, but minions cannot be forcefully moved across regions.
Each site will be flooded at the same moment as the minions arrive, so a submerged minion being evicted will also be submerged on the new site (and there will never be a moment where it's pushed onto the new site without the new site also being flooded).

question: When exactly does the previous site stop being flooded when I use this ability for the second time?
answer: The newly flooded site becomes flooded at the same moment the previously flooded site stops being flooded. If you choose the same site, there is no moment when the site isn't flood.

question: If the site doesn't get flooded (e.g. Bedrock), do the minions without submerge still tap?
answer: Yes! Imagine a big wave washing over the Bedrock, knocking everyone over, and then the water dissipates due to Bedrock.

question: Can I choose the same site over and over?
answer: Yes, as long as it's nearby your body of water.

question: Does the path include the starting and ending locations?
answer: Yes.

question: Can a unit with move-related abilities (e.g. Airborne) “take steps” using its ability?
answer: Yes.

question: Do I fully resolve my movement first, then strike each enemy simultaneously?
answer: Yes.

question: If I choose to move 0 steps (perhaps because my unit is Immobile), do I strike anything?
answer: No, because you don't have any path if you don't move. A path involves 1 or more steps, and each step has a starting and ending location that's different (if your step is from a location to the same location, you didn't actually move anywhere.)

question: Can I choose to move a step forward and then back to strike an enemy twice with this?
answer: No. You can choose to step forward and back, but an enemy is either along your path or not. They will not be struck more than once.

question: Can the White Hart's location be attacked?
answer: No, the White Hart's ability means that minions and locations which are nearby to the Hart, but are not the Hart, cannot be attacked. Everyone must focus on taking down the White Hart!

question: Does “visited before” apply to other Wildfires I cast in the same game?
answer: Once it leaves play, a Wildfire forgets all the places it visited. If you have multiple Wildfires in play, track them each separately.

question: If Wills-o’-the-Wisps are attacked and then use their ability to evade the attack, what happens?
answer: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends (assuming there aren't any units left to fight). The attacker will not strike, and the target of the attack will not revert to the original target (if any).

question: If Wills-o’-the-Wisps are attacked by a oversized minion, and then Wills-o’-the-Wisps teleport to a nearby location that the oversized minion still occupies, does the attack continue?
answer: Yes. To actually evade the attack, they must teleport to a location that the attacker doesn’t occupy.

question: Can I push something into the void?
answer: No. Since this is forced movement (and not normal unit movement), “one step” means a single adjacent location. (And “adjacent location” means an adjacent square in the same region.)

question: Per card text, artifacts that are carried get pushed as well. So, do held artifacts get blown away from the units carrying them?
answer: Since all of the movement is simultaneous the artifact always shares a location with the unit, so it was never dropped and continues to be carried.

question: If a weaker ally is attacked and you return them to your hand via this ability, what happens?
answer: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends, assuming there aren't any units left to fight. The attacker will not strike.

question: What does "Occupies all locations safely" mean?
answer: Yog Sothoth occupies all locations simultaneously, in all regions. That includes all surface locations, subsurface locations and voids. Yog Sothoth does not die due to being burrowed or submerged and is not banished due to being in the void.

question: What happens if there's a silence or disable effect somewhere in the realm that affects minions (e.g. Root Spider, Silence aura)?
answer: Yog-Sothoth will be disabled or silenced by the effect, but will continue to occupy all locations since its size is a characteristic. This usually means Yog-Sothoth will be banished, since it can no longer safely occupy void locations!
